name: ปศุสัตว์ Outbreak Investigator
idea: Helps a district livestock officer investigate a suspected livestock disease outbreak by tracing animal movements and vector risk.
twist: Draws the control and surveillance zones and drafts the movement-ban notice for the officer's approval.
sources: AgroSentinel (4th FAO-CAAS Youth Hackathon on One Health 2025, 3rd prize (New Service Track)) — Satellite-guided early warning system combining remote sensing and AI to monitor antimicrobial resistance and zoonotic disease risk on farms.
veTriage (OpenAI Build Week, 1st)

name: Withdrawal Period Gate
idea: Checks farm treatment records against each drug's withdrawal period before pigs or chickens are sent to slaughter.
twist: Asks the farm vet by voice to confirm any treatment missing from the log before release.
sources: Field Advisor (FAO Reboot the Earth Hackathon 2025, 2nd place, Rome) — Voice-powered RAG assistant giving farmers localized advice on crop selection, soil management and pest control for climate-resilient decisions.
veTriage (OpenAI Build Week, 1st)

name: 2Q·9Q·8Q Counsellor Copilot
idea: Helps a community-hospital nurse run Thai depression and suicide-risk screening, scoring it and routing per the local care pathway.
twist: Listens for risk cues in the patient's own words that contradict a low questionnaire score.
sources: AegisAI (AFTERKLASS Business KAMP 2025: Youth for Good (KBank), Thailand, 3rd) — AI agent app that provides emotional support and stress relief for women facing daily hardship.
One MIND (ก.พ.ร. Public Sector AI Hackathon 🇹🇭, 2nd)

name: Home Fall-Risk Assessor
idea: A caregiver photographs an older person's home; the tool flags fall hazards and proposes home modifications with costs.
twist: Prepares the request to the local long-term care fund in the format the sub-district office expects.
sources: Welli (OutSystems AI Agent Hackathon 2025 (Japan & Korea), Enterprise 1st) — Voice-based AI life-support app for seniors who face digital access barriers.

MaestrIA (Anthropic Built with Opus 4.7 Claude Code Hackathon 2026 (virtual), Keep Thinking Prize) — Home repair diagnostic tool that gives cost/time estimates and connects users with local skilled tradespeople.

name: ถุงยาเยี่ยมบ้าน · home med reconciliation
idea: A home-visit pharmacist photographs an older patient's bag of medicines; pills are identified and reconciled against hospital records.
twist: Spots duplicate drugs from different hospitals and expired stock hoarded at home.
sources: PillSnap (SGHackItRX 2025 (Pharmaceutical Society of Singapore), 1st Runner-up) — AI tool that detects and identifies multiple pills from one photo to help pharmacists with medication reconciliation.

name: Thai Braille Exam Transcriber
idea: Converts school exam papers, including maths and Thai tone marks, into Thai braille for special-education centres.
twist: Flags diagrams and tables that need tactile redrawing and writes alt descriptions for them.
sources: LUNA (MSIT AI Challenge & Hackathon 2025, Korea, Challenge Grand Prize) — AI-based braille translation solution for visually impaired users.

name: Accessible Building Auditor
idea: Checks photos and tape measurements of a public building's ramps, toilets and parking against Thai accessibility regulations.
twist: Ranks fixes by cost and impact for the building owner and drafts the response to the complaint.
sources: Hanamo (OutSystems AI Agent Hackathon 2025 (Japan & Korea), MVP Award) — Mobility safety support app for people with visual impairments.

Gemma Vision (Google Gemma 3n Impact Challenge 2025 (Kaggle, online), 1st place) — AI assistant for visually impaired people that processes chest-mounted phone camera visuals and responds to voice or controller commands.

name: ศูนย์ไกล่เกลี่ย Mediation Prep
idea: Prepares a court mediation file for consumer credit-card debt cases, summarising the claim, payments and realistic settlement options.
twist: Gives the mediator side-by-side instalment scenarios the debtor can afford based on stated income.
sources: Justi-Aid (Legal Hackathon Cologne 2025, 1st place, Germany) — AI-supported software that simplifies judicial processes and makes them more transparent for citizens.

Case Summary Workflow (Oxford Legal Tech Hackathon 2026 (BRYTER & Reed Smith), 2nd place, Oxford) — Turns uploaded court judgments into fact summaries, opinion comparisons, procedural timelines and answers to specific legal questions.

name: OPD Flow Twin
idea: Builds a digital twin of a provincial hospital's outpatient flow from queue timestamps to find where patients wait longest.
twist: Tests fixes such as moving lab draws earlier before the hospital changes anything.
sources: HospiTwin (MIT Hacking Medicine 2025, InterSystems Best Use of GenAI in Healthcare prize, Boston) — Digital twin of an emergency department floor that identifies the bottlenecks causing long patient wait times.

name: ประกันสังคม Appeal Drafter
idea: Explains a Social Security Office benefit rejection in plain Thai and drafts the worker's appeal with supporting documents.
twist: Points out which missing medical or employment evidence most likely caused the rejection.
sources: PlainRights (University of Auckland Legal Tech Hackathon 2025, 1st place, New Zealand) — Privacy-focused AI legal assistant that translates welfare-system legal documents into plain language and gives real-time guidance on users' rights.

name: Labour Inspector Visit Pack
idea: Prepares a labour inspector's workplace visit from complaints, past violations and payroll samples, with an interview checklist.
twist: Interviews migrant workers in their language and turns answers into the inspector's findings form.
sources: MigrAssist (Inter-University GenAI Hackathon for the SDGs 2025, Gold, Hong Kong) — Chatbot that helps migrant workers in Hong Kong understand their rights, track legal changes and connect with NGOs.

name: Alcohol Ad Checker
idea: Checks bar and restaurant social-media posts against Thai alcohol advertising restrictions before they are published.
twist: Explains which element is risky, such as drinking scenes or promotions, and suggests a compliant rewrite.
sources: Comply AI (Stanford LLM x Law Hackathon Fall 2024, Best First Build, Stanford) — Uses reasoning agents to check videos and digital communications against region-specific regulations, cutting compliance review from weeks to hours.

name: ACTD Dossier Checker
idea: Checks a generic drug registration dossier in ASEAN Common Technical Dossier format for missing or inconsistent parts before Thai FDA submission.
twist: Cross-checks strengths, shelf life and manufacturer names across modules to catch reviewer queries early.
sources: TrialIQ Agents (UiPath AgentHack 2025 (global, online), Grand Prize Agent of the Future) — Multi-agent clinical regulatory intelligence system aimed at accelerating drug approvals.

name: ไตอาหาร · renal diet planner
idea: Helps a hospital dietitian plan Thai meals for chronic kidney disease patients within potassium, phosphorus and protein targets.
twist: Suggests swaps for everyday Thai dishes and street food rather than unfamiliar Western menus.
sources: Healthfood Advisory (Alibaba Cloud Indonesia GenAI Hackathon 2025 (with GoTo), Indonesia, 2nd) — AI assistant inside GoFood that recommends healthy meals based on a user's dietary preferences and health goals.

name: ปภ. Situation Report Builder
idea: Merges district and village disaster reports into a provincial disaster office's standard situation report with affected-household counts.
twist: Detects duplicate or conflicting counts across districts before figures go to the governor.
sources: D-MIND (Super AI Engineer Season 5 2025, Thailand, AI Innovation Award) — Intelligent disaster monitoring and alert system built with AI.

MySelamat (Great Malaysia AI Hackathon 2025, Champion) — AI flood-response system that combines real-time crowdsourced social media data with AI rescue route planning via Google Maps to coordinate rescuers, victims and authorities.
